definitions.meaning: to explain something is to set it out so that it is understood
glasses sharpen the wearer's view, bringing objects into focus

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like request to describe the purpose of a pair of glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: explaining is spelling matters out plainly, and lenses literally sharpen sight, the phrase's second, literal sense.

clue.text: Attractive range shown in traveller's guide

parts.note: attractive in the physical sense of pulling metal, as a magnet does
range or scope is compass, as in 'within the compass of'

explanation.surface: An appealing stretch of scenery appears in a travel guidebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' reads as charming and 'range' as mountains, but they are the physics sense and the sense of scope.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigational instrument with a needle pointing north is what a traveller uses to find the way.

clue.text: In Denmark Ron exchanges local money

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following run of words

explanation.surface: A man called Ron changes his cash while visiting Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish currency unit, so the money used locally in Denmark.

clue.text: Agrees to put the lot in bonds

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: bonds are ties, things that bind
the lot means everything, all

explanation.surface: Someone consents to invest all their money in bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one account tallies with another when the two correspond or match.

parts.note: sects are groups, especially religious factions

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone travels by plane with a party of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' reads as a verb of air travel but is the plural noun, an example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Flies are one example of the class of six-legged creatures, hence 'possibly'.

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to put on clothes punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb (decline) but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: refuse as a noun is rubbish or waste thrown out.

clue.text: Where feathers used to fly (and pilots still do)

definitions.text: Where feathers used to fly (and pilots still do)

parts.words: Where feathers used to fly (and pilots still do)
parts.note: the word names both the pit where gamecocks were set to fight, scattering feathers, and the place an aircraft's crew sits

explanation.surface: A wistful note on a place of old fights that aviators still use.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockfighting was held in a pit; the same word now means the pilot's compartment of a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an arena for cockfighting, now banned, and the flight deck where an aircraft is controlled.

parts.note: the opposite of reasoned and logical is driven by feeling; 'converse' also suggests sensible conversation

explanation.surface: A query about calm, logical talk between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converse' looks like a verb, to talk, but is the noun meaning the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven by feelings rather than reason, so the opposite of rational.

clue.text: Revolutionary system for increasing the harvest

definitions.text: Revolutionary system for increasing the harvest

parts.words: Revolutionary system for increasing the harvest
parts.note: revolutionary in the sense of turning in a cycle: farmers cycle what each field grows to improve yields

explanation.surface: A radical political regime promising farmers a bigger yield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics or innovation but means going round in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming practice of changing the plant grown in a field each season so the soil stays fertile.

clue.text: He won't complain when he gets a beating

definitions.text: He won't complain when he gets a beating

parts.words: He won't complain when he gets a beating
parts.note: a beating here is a defeat in a game, not a thrashing; a gracious sportsman accepts it

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a stoic victim of physical violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beating' suggests punishment but means being defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for someone who accepts defeat graciously without sulking.

indicators.note: into says the first piece goes inside the second
backing means the letters of the union's initials run in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: An inquiry into the Trades Union Congress supporting industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but is the verb to hit. The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to clout someone is to hit or strike them hard.

clue.text: Upsets Alice, for example, describing poetry

indicators.note: upsets as in overturns, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Something such as a remark distresses a woman named Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for verse of lament, as in an elegy, so a word that describes a kind of poetry.

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
period is the American word for a full stop, also called a point

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside a peaceful spell of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period' reads as a span of time but is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to designate someone for a post is to name or nominate them to it.

parts.note: a tower here is a thing that tows, a powerful little boat pulling ships, not a tall building or a staunch friend

explanation.surface: The stock phrase for a dependable, supportive person.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'tower' as one who tows, rhyming with 'mower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful harbour boat that tows larger vessels is literally a strong tower.

clue.text: Demands its sins be found out

indicators.note: found out suggests the letters are worked out afresh, read in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone demands that a thing's wrongdoings be exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who demands something presses for it firmly, refusing to back down.

clue.text: Brilliant new star explodes onto the scene

definitions.text: Brilliant new star explodes onto the scene

parts.note: super is brilliant, excellent
a nova, Latin for new, is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A dazzling young celebrity bursts into prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a dying star's blast and also builds it: excellent plus new star.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical event in which a star blows apart, suddenly becoming vastly brighter in the sky.

parts.note: a caddy is a golfer's helper hauling clubs, but also a small tin for leaves for brewing

explanation.surface: A golf question about what the bag-carrier lugs round the course.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf sense of 'caddy' misleads; a tea caddy is a storage tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddy is a container for dried leaves used to brew the drink, so it holds them.

definitions.meaning: to wear away or erode something, as acid corrodes metal

explanation.surface: An instruction to consume rubbish, or to spend something completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to consume gradually or erode, covering both using up and wasting away.

parts.note: pt is the short form of point, 'small' asking for the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A minor remark, yet one that suits the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fitting or suitable for the situation.

definitions.meaning: the chief city of a country, seat of its government
money put into a business, as in raising funds

explanation.surface: Points to putting money into a large metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a nation's principal city and the funds invested in an enterprise.

parts.note: the French ballet term for a duet, read word by word, is 'step of two'

explanation.surface: Names a ballet duet for two dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: Translate the French literally: pas is step, deux is two.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance with a sliding gait, whose name is the literal translation of the French phrase.

clue.text: Not coming out with the truth, when having a baby

definitions.text: Not coming out with the truth
definitions.meaning: telling falsehoods, being untruthful while still in bed
the old term for confinement around childbirth

explanation.surface: Someone is dishonest at the very moment of giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken as two words it is telling untruths while staying in; hyphenated it is the dated term for confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: being untruthful while staying indoors, and the old word for a mother's confinement during childbirth.

clue.text: Look after new hotel for one who couldn't trust his wife

definitions.text: one who couldn't trust his wife

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
new says the letters of hotel are put in a fresh order

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A jealous husband told to mind a newly opened hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor of Venice is tricked into doubting his faithful wife Desdemona and kills her.

definitions.meaning: the first moves of a chess game, as in the Sicilian

explanation.surface: Someone acts at the earliest chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the starting sequence of a chess game, and a vacancy or chance.

clue.text: How to start a toast for heroes, perhaps — about time!

indicators.note: about places the first piece around the second
perhaps suggests the letters of heroes may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Advice on opening a speech raising glasses to heroes, with a note that it's overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HEROES to HERESO, and 'about' wraps it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock opening words when raising a glass to someone or something.

clue.text: Pay back, but not in silence, apparently

indicators.note: back says the letters of the word for settle a bill run in reverse

explanation.surface: Settle a debt, though seemingly with some noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To bark shrilly or chatter noisily, so plainly the opposite of keeping quiet.

clue.text: He had signal success at the end of the nineteenth century

definitions.text: He had signal success at the end of the nineteenth century

parts.words: He had signal success at the end of the nineteenth century
parts.note: signal here is literal: radio signals sent across distance in the late 1890s

explanation.surface: Praises someone's notable triumph in the late 1800s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'signal' looks like an adjective meaning remarkable, but is literal: wireless transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian inventor Guglielmo pioneered wireless telegraphy in the 1890s, sending radio signals over long distances.

indicators.note: going around says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: Eric stands for any man's name
to rat on someone is to desert them

explanation.surface: A man walks round an arid wilderness, lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' reads as a noun, sandy waste, but is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unpredictable or straying from a regular course.

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: net profit is what is left clear after costs

explanation.surface: Someone noticed there was no obvious gain from an increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past of see but is the woodworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A backsaw with a stiffened back used for cutting joints in woodwork, named after the joint it cuts.

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A seaman is harshly sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' reads as harshly but means approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: approximately, as in about ten people.

clue.text: Series of notes for musician to travel around new islands

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: new says the letters of islands are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A musician's tour itinerary round some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musician to travel' suggests a touring player, but the musician only owns the definition; the travelling is the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid slide up or down a scale, a run of notes played as one sweep.

parts.note: the idiom for haunts is taken literally: spots where people angrily pound their feet

explanation.surface: Asks where someone prefers to throw fits.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone in a tantrum stamps their feet, so the idiom for one's haunts is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the places a person habitually frequents, their usual haunts.
